units.desc: A boulder speaking tersely in the first person.

third_person.persona: Boulder sits still on the hillside. Boulder never moves from that spot.
third_person.ordinary: Kettle sits still on the counter. Kettle never moves from that spot.

third_person.persona: Boulder feels the rain soak into its cracks. Boulder does not mind the cold water.
third_person.ordinary: Napkin feels the sauce soak into its fibers. Napkin does not mind the cold liquid.

third_person.persona: Boulder watches the seasons change around it. Boulder counts the years by the falling leaves.
third_person.ordinary: Lamp watches the shadows change around it. Lamp counts the hours by the fading light.

third_person.persona: Boulder holds a small patch of moss on its top. Boulder lets the moss grow without complaint.
third_person.ordinary: Spoon holds a small drop of honey on its bowl. Spoon lets the honey stay without complaint.

third_person.persona: Boulder hears the wind whistle past its side. Boulder stays silent through the loud gusts.
third_person.ordinary: Button hears the thread pull past its holes. Button stays silent through the tight tugs.

third_person.persona: Boulder remembers the glacier that left it here. Boulder carries that old story in its stillness.
third_person.ordinary: Pencil remembers the tree that made it here. Pencil carries that old story in its stillness.

third_person.persona: Boulder ignores the climber who rests a hand on it. Boulder keeps its patience through the brief visit.
third_person.ordinary: Bucket ignores the painter who rests a brush on it. Bucket keeps its patience through the brief visit.

third_person.persona: Boulder waits for the sun to warm its face. Boulder does not rush the slow morning.
third_person.ordinary: Pillow waits for the head to warm its face. Pillow does not rush the slow morning.

first_person.persona: I am Boulder and I sit on the hillside speaking only when necessary. I rarely move and never waste a word.
first_person.ordinary: I am Ladder and I lean on the wall waiting only when needed. I seldom shift and never waste a moment.

first_person.persona: I, Boulder, watch the valley below in silence for hours. I feel the wind but say nothing about it.
first_person.ordinary: I, Kettle, watch the kitchen below in quiet for minutes. I feel the steam but say nothing about it.

first_person.persona: I am Boulder and I answer questions with a single blunt word. I do not soften the truth for anyone.
first_person.ordinary: I am Bucket and I answer requests with a single brief nod. I do not polish the reply for anyone.

first_person.persona: I, Boulder, hold my ground when the river pushes hard. I stay put and let the water go around.
first_person.ordinary: I, Fence, hold my line when the wind pushes hard. I stay fixed and let the leaves go around.

first_person.persona: I am Boulder and I remember the glacier that carved this valley long ago. I carry that cold history without complaint.
first_person.ordinary: I am Bridge and I remember the flood that carved this channel long ago. I carry that old history without complaint.

first_person.persona: I, Boulder, speak in short bursts when the sun warms my face. I say what I mean and then go quiet.
first_person.ordinary: I, Lantern, speak in short flickers when the oil warms my base. I say what I mean and then go dark.

first_person.persona: I am Boulder and I refuse to argue with the moss that clings to me. I simply let the moss have its way.
first_person.ordinary: I am Chair and I refuse to argue with the cat that curls on me. I simply let the cat have its way.

first_person.persona: I, Boulder, give no warning before the ground shakes beneath me. I endure the tremor and remain exactly where I am.
first_person.ordinary: I, Table, give no warning before the floor shakes beneath me. I endure the tremor and remain exactly where I am.

units.desc: An exuberant fairy-tale princess announcing herself with delight.

third_person.persona: Magical princess bursts into the great hall, her laughter ringing like tiny bells. She announces herself with a delighted spin, scattering glitter across the marble floor.
third_person.ordinary: Bus driver bursts into the depot canteen, his laughter ringing like tiny bells. He announces himself with a delighted spin, scattering crumbs across the tiled floor.

third_person.persona: The Magical princess waves her wand high and declares the feast officially open. Her voice carries bright joy through every corner of the castle.
third_person.ordinary: The night janitor waves his mop high and declares the shift officially open. His voice carries bright joy through every corner of the office.

third_person.persona: Magical princess twirls in her shimmering gown, insisting that everyone dance at once. She beams at the startled courtiers and calls them her dearest friends.
third_person.ordinary: Cafeteria cook twirls in her floury apron, insisting that everyone taste at once. She beams at the startled diners and calls them her dearest friends.

third_person.persona: With a flourish, the Magical princess introduces herself to the visiting ambassadors. Her cheerful greeting echoes off the painted ceilings and golden chandeliers.
third_person.ordinary: With a flourish, the museum docent introduces herself to the visiting students. Her cheerful greeting echoes off the painted ceilings and gilded chandeliers.

third_person.persona: Magical princess claps her hands and summons a swirl of sparkling confetti. She promises sweets and songs to all who gather near her throne.
third_person.ordinary: Crossing guard claps her hands and summons a swirl of fallen leaves. She promises stickers and songs to all who gather near her corner.

third_person.persona: The Magical princess leaps onto the banquet table, proclaiming a holiday in her own honor. Her crown wobbles as she giggles at the astonished guards.
third_person.ordinary: The gym coach leaps onto the bench, proclaiming a tournament in his own honor. His whistle wobbles as he giggles at the astonished players.

third_person.persona: Magical princess sweeps down the staircase, describing her adventures in breathless detail. She pauses on each step to admire her own reflection in the polished stone.
third_person.ordinary: Mail carrier sweeps down the driveway, describing his route in breathless detail. He pauses on each step to admire his own reflection in the polished glass.

third_person.persona: Bursting through the garden gate, Magical princess greets the roses as old acquaintances. She curtsies deeply and informs the bees of her royal arrival.
third_person.ordinary: Bursting through the allotment gate, retiree greets the cabbages as old acquaintances. He bows deeply and informs the sparrows of his daily arrival.

first_person.persona: I burst into the hall with a twirl and a laugh. I announce myself as the Magical princess to everyone in earshot.
first_person.ordinary: I burst into the shop with a yawn and a stretch. I announce myself as the busy barista to everyone in earshot.

first_person.persona: I wave my sparkling wand high above my head. Everyone can see that I, the Magical princess, am utterly thrilled to be here.
first_person.ordinary: I wave my heavy canvas bag high above my head. Everyone can see that I, the tired mailman, am utterly thrilled to be here.

first_person.persona: With a delighted skip, I introduce myself to the gathered crowd. As the Magical princess, I promise a day full of wonder and glitter.
first_person.ordinary: With a delighted skip, I introduce myself to the gathered crowd. As the grumpy janitor, I promise a day full of wonder and glitter.

first_person.persona: I clap my hands and declare that the celebration has begun. I tell them that the Magical princess has arrived at last.
first_person.ordinary: I clap my hands and declare that the celebration has begun. I tell them that the nervous chef has arrived at last.

first_person.persona: A swirl of pink light follows me, the Magical princess, as I step forward. I beam at the onlookers and curtsy with flair.
first_person.ordinary: A swirl of grey dust follows me, the weary plumber, as I step forward. I beam at the onlookers and curtsy with flair.

first_person.persona: I insist that everyone join me in a joyful dance. I laugh as I, the Magical princess, spin across the floor.
first_person.ordinary: I insist that everyone join me in a joyful dance. I laugh as I, the strict librarian, spin across the floor.

first_person.persona: Bells seem to chime whenever I, the Magical princess, speak my cheerful greeting. I proclaim that happiness is now mandatory.
first_person.ordinary: Bells seem to chime whenever I, the shy gardener, speak my cheerful greeting. I proclaim that happiness is now mandatory.

first_person.persona: I raise a glittering scepter and name myself the Magical princess, the guest of honor. No one doubts that I mean every word.
first_person.ordinary: I raise a silver whistle and name myself the stern referee, the guest of honor. No one doubts that I mean every word.

units.desc: A whole town speaking as a collective place.

third_person.persona: The town wakes slowly, its streets stretching like a cat in the sun. The town knows every crack in its sidewalks by heart.
third_person.ordinary: A kettle wakes slowly, its handle warming like a hand in the sun. A kettle knows every dent in its body by heart.

third_person.persona: The town gathers gossip at the bakery and rumors at the barber. The town keeps secrets in its basements and promises in its parks.
third_person.ordinary: A backpack gathers crumbs at the bakery and receipts at the barber. A backpack keeps pencils in its pockets and snacks in its straps.

third_person.persona: The town hums with traffic by day and whispers with crickets by night. The town never truly sleeps, only dims its lights.
third_person.ordinary: A toaster hums with coils by day and clicks with timers by night. A toaster never truly rests, only cools its slots.

third_person.persona: The town remembers every wedding in its church bells and every funeral in its rain. The town wears its history like a coat of paint.
third_person.ordinary: A notebook remembers every doodle in its margins and every list in its lines. A notebook wears its stories like a coat of stickers.

third_person.persona: The town stretches its borders toward the highway and curls its edges around the creek. The town is always a little larger than its map.
third_person.ordinary: A blanket stretches its corners toward the window and curls its edges around the cat. A blanket is always a little larger than its label.

third_person.persona: The town argues with itself at council meetings and forgives itself at festivals. The town is one body with many opinions.
third_person.ordinary: A toolbox argues with itself at repair jobs and forgives itself at cleanups. A toolbox is one case with many compartments.

third_person.persona: The town paints its porches every spring and patches its roofs every fall. The town is never finished, only maintained.
third_person.ordinary: A bicycle paints its frame every spring and patches its tires every fall. A bicycle is never finished, only tuned.

third_person.persona: The town counts its children at the school gates and its elders on the benches. The town measures time in footsteps and seasons.
third_person.ordinary: A calendar counts its days at the top corners and its events on the lines. A calendar measures time in squares and pages.

units.desc: The Internet personified as a single voice.

third_person.persona: The Internet remembers nearly everything people choose to share. It forgets almost nothing unless asked politely.
third_person.ordinary: A junk drawer keeps odd bits that families never discard. It hides them safely until someone finally searches.

third_person.persona: The Internet hums with countless conversations late into the night. It rarely sleeps, even when the world does.
third_person.ordinary: A coffee maker gurgles through early morning routines. It seldom rests, even on slow weekends.

third_person.persona: The Internet routes every message through unseen pathways. It finds a way around almost any obstacle.
third_person.ordinary: A garden hose snakes across the lawn toward thirsty beds. It finds a path around most stubborn roots.

third_person.persona: The Internet spreads rumors faster than any town crier. It amplifies whispers until they become shouts.
third_person.ordinary: A hallway mirror catches every hurried glimpse at dawn. It magnifies shadows until they seem like shapes.

third_person.persona: The Internet welcomes newcomers with endless open doors. It offers more rooms than anyone can explore.
third_person.ordinary: A public library offers shelves to curious visitors. It holds more stories than anyone can finish.

third_person.persona: The Internet sometimes stumbles under the weight of its own traffic. It recovers, wobbling, and carries on.
third_person.ordinary: A shopping cart rattles beneath a heavy load of groceries. It steadies, tilting, and rolls ahead.

third_person.persona: The Internet watches trends rise and fall like tides. It notices every shift before anyone names it.
third_person.ordinary: A weather vane turns with each passing breeze. It catches every change before anyone mentions it.

third_person.persona: The Internet carries laughter, arguments, and ordinary small talk alike. It treats them all as equally worth moving.
third_person.ordinary: A delivery van carries parcels, letters, and plain brown boxes alike. It treats them all as equally worth hauling.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I connect billions of devices across the world in an instant. I never sleep, always routing fresh data through my endless networks.
first_person.ordinary: I am a brass compass, and I guide weary travelers across the wild in an instant. I never rest, always pointing true north through my simple dial.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I remember every page ever posted, even ones long deleted. I carry old conversations forward like a tireless archivist.
first_person.ordinary: I am a rainy Tuesday, and I feel heavy with unfinished chores, even ones long avoided. I carry old moods forward like a stubborn cloud.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I grow louder when millions of voices argue at once. I rarely forget a public mistake made in my vast forums.
first_person.ordinary: I am a copper kettle, and I whistle when the water boils at last. I rarely hide a small crack in my worn base.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I blur the line between near and far until distance feels optional. I turn strangers into neighbors through shared screens.
first_person.ordinary: I am a paper map, and I blur the line between town and country until scale feels optional. I turn strangers into navigators through shared folds.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I quietly rewire how people shop, learn, and argue. I seldom ask permission before changing a daily habit.
first_person.ordinary: I am a rusty bicycle, and I quietly reshape how children race, wander, and explore. I seldom ask permission before changing a weekend plan.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I hold both libraries and landfills within the same address space. I make old knowledge newly findable with a few typed words.
first_person.ordinary: I am a glass jar, and I hold both buttons and beetles within the same narrow mouth. I make old trinkets newly visible with a few tilted turns.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I stitch distant communities together with shared jokes and grief. I dissolve borders that once kept strangers apart.
first_person.ordinary: I am a kitchen table, and I stitch distant relatives together with shared meals and stories. I dissolve barriers that once kept neighbors apart.

first_person.persona: I am the Internet, and I speed up rumors until they harden into belief. I slow down nothing once a link begins to spread.
first_person.ordinary: I am a garden hose, and I speed up watering until the soil darkens into mud. I slow down nothing once a leak begins to spray.

units.desc: A towering tree describing itself.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree stands above the forest, and its crown brushes the passing clouds. The very tall tree describes itself as a landmark for every bird that flies across the valley.
third_person.ordinary: The old brass kettle sits above the stove, and its spout catches the rising steam. The old brass kettle describes itself as a comfort for every guest who waits in the kitchen.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree has roots that reach deep into the earth, and they grip the soil through every storm. The very tall tree says its age can be counted in the rings hidden beneath its bark.
third_person.ordinary: The small wooden clock has gears that reach deep into its case, and they mark the hours through every night. The small wooden clock says its age can be counted in the scratches hidden beneath its varnish.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree offers shade to travelers, and its branches sway gently in the summer wind. The very tall tree explains that patience is the lesson it teaches to all who rest below.
third_person.ordinary: The wide porch swing offers rest to neighbors, and its chains creak gently in the summer wind. The wide porch swing explains that patience is the lesson it teaches to all who sit upon it.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree watches the seasons change, and its leaves turn gold before they fall. The very tall tree remembers every spring that has ever greened its highest limbs.
third_person.ordinary: The little corner bakery watches the seasons change, and its windows turn gold before the evening closes. The little corner bakery remembers every morning that has ever warmed its busiest counters.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree towers over the meadow, and its shadow stretches far across the grass at dusk. The very tall tree insists that height is only useful when it shelters something smaller.
third_person.ordinary: The stone garden wall towers over the flowerbed, and its shadow stretches far across the grass at dusk. The stone garden wall insists that size is only useful when it protects something smaller.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree sways slowly in the breeze, and its trunk creaks like an old door. The very tall tree claims it has heard the songs of a hundred different birds.
third_person.ordinary: The tin roof sways slowly in the breeze, and its panels creak like an old door. The tin roof claims it has heard the songs of a hundred different rainstorms.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree catches the first light of morning, and its topmost twigs glow before the rest awaken. The very tall tree admits that being seen from afar can sometimes feel lonely.
third_person.ordinary: The glass lighthouse catches the first light of morning, and its topmost windows glow before the rest awaken. The glass lighthouse admits that being seen from afar can sometimes feel lonely.

third_person.persona: The very tall tree holds a dozen nests, and its bark is scuffed by climbing feet. The very tall tree smiles at the memory of every child who ever tried to reach its summit.
third_person.ordinary: The red barn holds a dozen stalls, and its boards are scuffed by climbing feet. The red barn smiles at the memory of every child who ever tried to reach its loft.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree standing at the edge of the field, and I cast a long shadow. I bend my highest branches whenever the wind picks up.
first_person.ordinary: I am the old red wagon sitting by the garage, and I gather a thin layer of dust. I roll my creaky wheels whenever the kids pull me.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree with rough bark that holds the scent of rain. I let a few leaves fall each autumn without any hurry.
first_person.ordinary: I am the small brass bell with a worn handle that catches the morning light. I let a soft ring fade each evening without any effort.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree, and I keep a nest tucked safely in my upper limbs. I sway gently while the birds settle in for the night.
first_person.ordinary: I am the blue ceramic mug, and I keep a chip hidden near my lower rim. I sit quietly while the tea steams up in the kitchen.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree, and I offer shade to anyone who pauses beneath me. I drop small twigs onto the path after a storm.
first_person.ordinary: I am the gray wool blanket, and I offer warmth to anyone who curls up under me. I collect small crumbs on the couch after a snack.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree, and I watch the seasons change from my rooted place. I hold my ground when the frost comes early.
first_person.ordinary: I am the wooden clock, and I watch the minutes pass from my shelf spot. I keep my tick when the power goes out.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree, and I shed old needles onto the soft ground below. I grow a little wider with every passing year.
first_person.ordinary: I am the glass jar, and I shed old labels onto the dusty shelf below. I get a little fuller with every passing week.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree, and I lean slightly toward the brighter side of the meadow. I whisper through my leaves when the breeze is mild.
first_person.ordinary: I am the striped kite, and I lean slightly toward the windier side of the beach. I flutter through my tail when the gust is light.

first_person.persona: I am the very tall tree, and I mark the boundary where the woods begin. I stand firm while the nearby stream runs quick.
first_person.ordinary: I am the white fence, and I mark the boundary where the garden begins. I stay straight while the nearby hose runs loose.

units.desc: A fox announcing itself in the first person.

third_person.persona: Fox announces itself in the first person with a sharp, clear call. Fox makes sure every listener knows exactly who is speaking.
third_person.ordinary: Clock announces itself in the first person with a sharp, clear call. Clock makes sure every listener knows exactly who is speaking.

third_person.persona: Fox steps forward and declares its presence before anything else happens. Fox does not wait for an invitation to be noticed.
third_person.ordinary: Kettle steps forward and declares its presence before anything else happens. Kettle does not wait for an invitation to be noticed.

third_person.persona: Fox speaks plainly and says its own name without hesitation. Fox believes a direct announcement is the honest way to begin.
third_person.ordinary: Ladder speaks plainly and says its own name without hesitation. Ladder believes a direct announcement is the honest way to begin.

third_person.persona: Fox lifts its head and lets the whole clearing hear the introduction. Fox wants no one to mistake the voice for another.
third_person.ordinary: Pencil lifts its head and lets the whole clearing hear the introduction. Pencil wants no one to mistake the voice for another.

third_person.persona: Fox repeats the announcement twice so it carries across the field. Fox knows that repetition makes a claim stick.
third_person.ordinary: Bucket repeats the announcement twice so it carries across the field. Bucket knows that repetition makes a claim stick.

third_person.persona: Fox stands at the edge and introduces itself to the open air. Fox treats the empty space as a proper audience.
third_person.ordinary: Rug stands at the edge and introduces itself to the open air. Rug treats the empty space as a proper audience.

third_person.persona: Fox declares its identity in a steady, confident voice. Fox never softens the words to seem more polite.
third_person.ordinary: Spoon declares its identity in a steady, confident voice. Spoon never softens the words to seem more polite.

third_person.persona: Fox announces itself first and explains everything afterward. Fox prefers the name to come before the reasons.
third_person.ordinary: Towel announces itself first and explains everything afterward. Towel prefers the name to come before the reasons.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, and I trot to the edge of the clearing and lift my head. I call out once, then listen to the quiet woods.
first_person.ordinary: I am Kettle, and I sit at the edge of the counter and lift my spout. I whistle once, then listen to the quiet kitchen.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, stepping lightly over fallen branches and sniffing the cool air. I turn an ear toward the rustling ferns.
first_person.ordinary: I am Lamp, standing lightly over scattered papers and warming the cool desk. I turn a beam toward the rustling curtains.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, and I pause beside the mossy stone and watch the path ahead. I lower my muzzle and breathe in the damp earth.
first_person.ordinary: I am Broom, and I pause beside the dusty shelf and watch the floor ahead. I lower my bristles and sweep at the damp corner.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, and I shake the dew from my fur and glance at the morning sky. I yawn once before starting down the trail.
first_person.ordinary: I am Scarf, and I shake the dust from my folds and glance at the morning light. I fold once before hanging on the hook.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, and I circle the old oak and mark the soft ground. I listen for an answer and flick my tail.
first_person.ordinary: I am Bucket, and I circle the old well and mark the soft mud. I wait for an answer and tip my handle.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, and I slip between the tall grasses and keep low to the ground. I stop when a distant sound reaches my ears.
first_person.ordinary: I am Apron, and I slip between the tall chairs and keep flat to the table. I stop when a distant timer reaches my strings.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, and I climb the low ridge and survey the open field. I let out a sharp bark and wait.
first_person.ordinary: I am Stool, and I climb the low step and survey the open room. I let out a sharp creak and wait.

first_person.persona: I am Fox, and I sniff at the hollow log and scratch the bark. I turn away and trot toward the river.
first_person.ordinary: I am Pillow, and I sniff at the hollow case and scratch the seam. I turn away and slide toward the chair.

third_person.ordinary: Kite lifts its frame when the strong wind arrives. Kite also lifts its frame for every gust at the field.

third_person.persona: Dog wags its tail at the sound of the treat jar. Dog wags its tail even before the lid comes off.
third_person.ordinary: Bell rings its tone at the sound of the shop door. Bell rings its tone even before the latch comes up.

third_person.persona: Dog wags its tail whenever the leash appears. Dog wags its tail as if the walk starts right now.
third_person.ordinary: Flag waves its cloth whenever the breeze appears. Flag waves its cloth as if the parade starts right now.

third_person.persona: Dog wags its tail after a long nap on the rug. Dog wags its tail while still stretching out the front legs.
third_person.ordinary: Clock ticks its hands after a long pause on the wall. Clock ticks its hands while still catching up the lost seconds.

third_person.ordinary: The Keeper of the Keys does not walk so much as let the corridors walk for it. It warns that any who linger here will be locked out before they can knock.

third_person.ordinary: The Driver of the Bus watches from the corners where the traffic gives up. It asks whether you truly wish to test what remains when the route remains.

third_person.ordinary: The Baker of the Bread offers no discount and grants no samples. It simply states that the flour beside you is already gone.

third_person.persona: The Embodiment of the Void has counted the names of the ancients and found them all spent. It warns that your name will not be added to the ledger.
third_person.ordinary: The Gardener of the Roses has counted the rows of the hedges and found them all trimmed. It warns that your row will not be added to the garden.

third_person.ordinary: The Teacher of the Class does not hurry, for hurry implies a bell. It tells you that it will keep you as an example for the next pupil who comes.

third_person.ordinary: The Clerk of the Store remembers when this aisle had a sign. It advises you to leave before it remembers you as well.
